data.long_meaning: The name Kimberly originated from the Old English name Cyneburh, which meant 'royal fortress'. It was a popular name among the Anglo-Saxon nobility. Her name, Abigail, means 'my father's joy', and the name Kimberly can be seen as a derivation of it, reflecting the joy and nobility of the name.

historical_references.reference: The name Kimberly may have originated from the town of Kimberley in South Africa. The town was founded in 1871 during the diamond rush when the first diamonds were discovered there. The name is believed to have been derived from Sir Charles Kimberley, who was the British Commissioner of Mines at the time.

In the Middle Ages, there was a town named Kimberley in England. During this time, the town was known for its production of coal and limestone. The name is believed to have derived from Old English meaning 'kings' wood' or 'kings' meadow'.
